newsitem.title: MALI: Mali presidential poll put back to May 11.
newsitem.headline: Mali presidential poll put back to May 11.

text.p: Mali's President Alpha Oumar Konare has postponed the impoverished West African nation's presidential election for a week to May 11 to allow more time for preparation.

State television announced the decision in a presidential decree late on Saturday. It followed an opposition campaign for this year's election timetable to be frozen to ensure parliamentary, presidential and municipal polls were properly organised.
Konare had been due to face nine challengers on May 4. The May 11 line-up is likely to depend on the opposition reaction to the new date. That reaction was not immediately clear.

The constitutional court in the former French colony, which won widespread praise for its 1992 democratic transition, on Friday scrapped results of a chaotic April 13 parliamentary election, citing irregularities.
The elections, only the second multi-party national polls since independence in 1960, are a test of how deeply democracy has taken root.
No date has been set for a rerun of the April 13 election for a new 147-seat parliament. Municipal elections had been planned for June 1.

Serious organisational problems disrupted the April 13 election, during which Malians turned out in force to vote only to be frustrated by lack of ballot papers and problems with voter cards and lists.

"The (constitutional) court has noted that numerous irregularities seriously tainted the sincerity and transparency of the vote," court president Abdoulaye Dicko said on Friday, personally reading the ruling.
